name: ENS-PSL International Selection (École Normale Supérieure - PSL)
requiredDocuments: Detailed editable application form (downloaded from ENS, filled out)
High school diploma (in French or English; Spanish, Italian or Portuguese also accepted)
University transcript (in French or English; Spanish, Italian or Portuguese also accepted)

Motivation/cover letter, 1 to 3 pages (Times New Roman, 12 pt, 1.5 spacing) — in French for Arts & Humanities (also in English for Economics, Linguistics, Cognitive studies); in French OR English for Sciences
Arts & Humanities only: a research/study project of max 3 pages (10,000 characters incl. spaces) with a bibliography of 10 books
2 to 4 letters of recommendation (any format accepted)
All documents merged into a single PDF named 'Family Name-Given Name.pdf' (do NOT include a passport or ID card)

timeline.deadline: Arts & Humanities: 3 December 2025, 12:00 midday Paris time; Sciences: 15 December 2025, 12:00 midday Paris time
timeline.resultsBy: Admission results from 4 March 2026 (Arts & Humanities) / from 26 March 2026 (Sciences)
timeline.notes: Dates are the 2026-entry cycle (applications Oct–Dec 2025), as published on the official page (last updated 18/02/2026). As of the 2026-06 anchor the next cycle had not opened; the program runs on a fixed annual calendar (apply in autumn, tests Feb–Mar, entry in autumn). Shortlist/tests: A&H written tests 2–6 Feb 2026 and oral tests 9–13 Feb 2026; Sciences tests 3–20 March 2026 — all conducted remotely by videoconference.

benefits: Monthly grant of €1,000 paid for 36 months (3 years)
Right to request a furnished room on an ENS campus (rue d'Ulm, boulevard Jourdan, or Montrouge); rent ~€315/month
Tuition in French public universities paid by the French State (student pays only modest annual registration/inscription fees + CVEC)
Free French language courses throughout the year, plus an intensive course at the start of September
Graduate with both a Master's degree (M1+M2) in the chosen specialty and the diploma of the École normale supérieure (DENS)

acceptanceRate.source: ENS-PSL official FAQ: 'How hard is the selection? The selection rates varies from year to year, between 5 and 10%.' https://www.ens.psl.eu/en/une-formation-d-exception/admissions/international/international-selection/faq-about-international (accessed 2026-06-18)

mustKnow: Strict age limit: you must apply before turning 26 (Arts & Humanities: not past your 26th birthday on 1 December; Sciences: under 26 on the application opening day).
Two-step competitive examination: first a selection on dossier, then remote (videoconference) written and oral tests for shortlisted candidates — this is a concours, not a simple admissions review.
You can apply to the International Selection ONLY ONCE in your life — former candidates' files are not transmitted to the jury.

Requires at least one year of undergraduate study at a FOREIGN (non-French) university now, and two years by the September after admission — a Bangladeshi who studied in Bangladesh qualifies; there is no nationality restriction.
Residence rule: must not have lived in France more than 10 months (Arts & Humanities) / 6 months (Sciences) during the selection year and the year before.

Fully funded with a living stipend (€1,000/month for 36 months) PLUS state-paid tuition — but the grant is not paid during any gap year, and ENS can only pay it into a French bank account you must open on arrival.

No ten-year State-service commitment: International Selection students receive a grant (not a salary) and do not become civil servants, so unlike regular normaliens they are NOT bound by the ten-year engagement — effectively no return-home/service bond.

Arts & Humanities is taught and tested mainly in French (B1 reading/writing recommended, no official certificate required); Sciences departments teach in French or English and no language level is officially required — so no IELTS/TOEFL is demanded.
Enrollment in both a Master's and the ENS graduate degree (DENS, 72 extra ECTS over 3 years) is compulsory.

duration: 3 years (M1+M2 Master plus 72 ECTS for the ENS graduate degree / DENS)
eligibleNationalities: Open to all nationalities worldwide (no country restriction); requires at least one year (ultimately two years) of undergraduate study at a foreign/non-French university and a France-residence cap. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible.
languageRequirements: No official language certificate required. Arts & Humanities: courses and most tests in French — candidates should read/write French at roughly B1 level. Sciences: courses in French or English depending on department; no language level officially required. No IELTS/TOEFL demanded.
standardizedTests: Not required (selection is via ENS's own written and oral competitive tests, not GRE/GMAT)
ageLimit: Under 26 — must apply before turning 26 (Arts & Humanities: not past 26th birthday on 1 December; Sciences: under 26 on opening day of applications)
applicationFee: Free (no application fee stated on the official page)
fundingCovers: On-campus accommodation (room available, rent ~€315/month paid from grant)
Tuition (state-paid; only modest annual registration/inscription fees + CVEC remain)
bondObligation: None — International Selection students receive a grant (not a salary), do not become civil servants, and are not subject to the ten-year State-service commitment.
renewalConditions: Grant paid over 3 years; must remain enrolled in a Master's and the ENS graduate degree (DENS, 72 ECTS over 3 years). Grant is suspended during any gap year/semester (up to 2 gap years permitted).
postStudyWork: Graduates hold a French Master's degree plus the ENS diploma; standard French post-study work/residence options apply (admitted students enter on a 'visa long séjour pour études' arranged via Campus France). No program-specific stay-back scheme stated.
